notes_for_editor: NRHP nomination PDF is not digitised (22 KB placeholder), so only the NPGallery metadata was used. Appropriation: the 1899 report's OCR prints $16,000, later documents $15,000; the story says so. Completion date: LighthouseFriends 25 June 1904, Pepper 15 June 1904. Tower height: LighthouseFriends/USLHS 75 ft, Pepper 57 ft foundation to ventilator ball. Site: Board proposed NW end in 1891-92; Pepper says survey chose the SE point (single source, copyrighted, paraphrased). Light-lit conflict: LighthouseFriends says original characteristic kept; USLHS record has active_aton false and open_to_public false. The 1912 Bulletin item on Jensen is two interleaved OCR columns; read as 'Niels P. Jensen, first assistant keeper of St. Martin Island Light Station, Wis., has been commended for saving six motor boats from destruction by fire'. The 1913 Cepheus grounding: Bulletin says tender pulled her off 10 Oct; Evening Star ties it to the 'recent storm'; not tied to keepers, kept short. Imperial Valley Press 12 Nov 1913 is an unclear wire dispatch on the Plymouth. Roster is from USLHS (NARA registers via Anderson); Royal G. Peterson (USLHS) vs Roy G. Peterson (LighthouseFriends), Pizzala vs Pizzalar. LighthouseFriends 'Wis.' appears in some Bulletin entries for the island (it is in Michigan). Footnote 8 USLHS roster also supports Lockhart service dates. No reports for fiscal 1902-1911 are in the corpus, so the 1902-1905 construction years rest on LighthouseFriends and Pepper. Fadel dates by LighthouseFriends; Lockhart 'thirty-four years of service' is total service, not at this station only (LighthouseFriends says he came in 1946, USLHS head keeper from 1947). Checker 2026-10-27: railway completion 1864 (Pepper) vs 1865 (LighthouseFriends); station location northeastern side (LighthouseFriends) vs southeast point (Pepper); Pizzala stayed as first assistant 1917-1920; Cepheus 10 October Bulletin date and the November newspaper 'recent storm' may be different events.
